LESSON: WATER HARDNESS

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: INTEGRATED SCIENCE
Strand: Mixtures, Elements, and Compounds
Topic 1.3: Water hardness

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Water hardness
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: What are the uses of water?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. name uses of water at home and school
2. explain why clean water is important
3. show ways to conserve water
4. practise safe water habits

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ What is water?

• Water is a natural resource we need every day.
• We find water in taps, rivers, lakes, tanks, and rain.

▸ Uses of water

Teach
• List uses under Home and School.

Worked example
• Home: drinking, cooking ugali/sukuma, bathing, washing clothes, cleaning utensils.
• School: drinking, washing hands, cleaning classrooms, watering gardens.
• Farm/community: watering crops, animals drinking.

Try this
• Draw 4 pictures: drink, wash hands, cook, water a plant. Label each.
• Say 3 uses of water at your home.

▸ Why clean water matters

Teach
• Dirty water can make us sick.
• Clean covered water is safer to drink.

Worked example
• Safe: water from a clean covered container / treated tap water.
• Unsafe: open dirty puddle water for drinking.

Try this
• Which is safer for drinking: covered tank water or open puddle? Why?
• (Check later: Covered tank/treated water — less germs)

▸ Conserve water (do not waste)

Teach
• Close the tap when soaping hands.
• Report leaking taps.
• Use a basin instead of a running tap when washing.

Worked example
• Bad habit: leaving a tap running while brushing teeth.
• Good habit: fill a cup, close tap, brush, rinse.

Try this
• List 3 ways you will save water this week at home.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• Uses: drinking, cooking, washing, farming
• Safe storage: covered clean container
• Save water: close taps, fix leaks

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Name 5 uses of water.
2. Tick safe vs unsafe drinking sources.
3. Act out: washing hands the correct way (wet → soap → scrub → rinse → close tap).

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Make a water-saving poster for your class.
2. Teach a younger child: “Close the tap.”

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What are the uses of water?
2. How do we conserve water?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Water is useful at home and school.
• Drink clean safe water.
• Do not waste water.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
